works.title: Masoretic Text (Tanakh)
works.statusBasis: A collection: each book has its own record and status.
works.notes: Hebrew, with Aramaic in Daniel 2:4b–7:28, Ezra 4:8–6:18 and 7:12–26, Jeremiah 10:11 and two words of Genesis 31:47. The text is the codex as written (ketiv); the marginal readings (qere) are in notes, which are not taken.

Etheridge's 1862 volume carries Genesis-Exodus (Internet Archive record); the 1865 second volume (Leviticus-Deuteronomy) is stated in the owner's brief and was not itself opened. The targum.info index links Onkelos to the whole Pentateuch: Genesis 12 pages, Exodus 11, Leviticus 9, Numbers 10 and Deuteronomy as one page. Sefaria's Aramaic versions (Torat Emet "Onkelos Genesis" etc., and the Hebrew Wikisource Yemenite text) cover all five books with matching segment counts. Mechon Mamre also has Onkelos but allows private study only. CAL holds the text base; no licence found. The original role is proposed as the Taj text with rights unverified, so the work is held at english_public_domain_only until the Aramaic role is settled.

No openly licensed machine-readable Armenian text was found, so original is null. If one is later found, file it with language 'armenian'. Robinson's introduction and notes are his own 1920 work.

works.notes: The Vulgate is not Jerome's alone: the Clementine Vulgate contains Jerome's new translation from the Hebrew (most of the OT), his Gallican Psalter, his revision of the Gospels, and Old Latin books he did not revise (Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus, Baruch, Maccabees, most of the NT outside the Gospels, and others) - a point from general knowledge, not read on a page this session. The Latin Wikisource page also contains Jerome's prefaces ('Hieronymi praefationes' sub-pages, in source.pages) and the Clementine Project's own modern prefaces (hence 'modern-introduction': the ingest must leave out 'Approbatio (2006)' and 'Praefatio hujus editionis (2004)'). English: Douay-Rheims is a translation OF the Vulgate, not a translation by Jerome; Challoner's 1749-52 revision is the text printed in 1914. NPNF II vol. 6 prints Jerome's prefaces in English (a separate item, not the Bible text).
